items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: Nothing is recommended, and L's weak axes are visible: 870 ms pooled, a 0.3-point multi-hop clearance, the best of eighteen. The watch slot applies an inference to L alone. That inference puts about 300 multi-hop cases behind L's clearance, a fraction of one SE and close to even odds. The same inference puts about 180 ambiguous-entity cases behind J's 0.6-point miss (SE about 1.4 points, so about 0.4 SE). That miss is as likely to be noise as L's clearance, yet our_lean states it as a firm miss ('misses only the pass line ... by 1.4 points in multi-hop and 0.6 in ambiguous entities'). Read with the same treatment, J's only firm-looking miss is multi-hop, at about 1.2 SE. That bears directly on the L-or-J question put to the owner. Separately, where_it_flips offers routing as a way to 'meet both lines with neither moved' without saying what the pooled figure demands of it. If L held 600 ms in multi-hop and ambiguous entities (40% of traffic), at most 2% of all calls could exceed 870 ms from those tasks. L's pooled p95 of 870 ms then needs its single-lookup and date-math p95 to be at least about 870 ms: the reverse of the watch slot's own expectation that multi-hop runs slowest.

findings.finding: The noise treatment of the two near options is asymmetric. The watch slot's inference (cases drawn by traffic share) makes L's 0.3-point multi-hop clearance about 0.3 SE on about 300 cases. By the same inference, J's 0.6-point ambiguous-entity miss (criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.disamb.gap) is about 0.4 SE on about 180 cases, equally fragile. Only J's 1.4-point multi-hop miss is about 1.2 SE. our_lean and next item 4 present both of J's misses as firm. State the same labelled inference for J, so the owner sees that J's shortfall rests mainly on multi-hop, just as L's clearance rests on a coin flip there.

The routing option in where_it_flips (and next items 1 and 3) is offered as a way to 'meet both lines with neither moved' without saying what the pooled latency already demands of it. L's pooled p95 is 870 ms (measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95). For L to hold 600 ms in multi-hop and ambiguous entities (25% + 15% of traffic), those tasks could put at most 2% of all calls over 870 ms. Single lookup and date math, the tasks routed to J, would then need L's own p95 there to be at least about 870 ms. That is the reverse of the watch slot's expectation that multi-hop runs slowest. Say this in one sentence where routing is offered, so it doesn't read as live as the in-between Brisk-S run.
